exposure: mode of delivery (caesarean section, vaginal delivery)
cohort: 100 postnatal mothers (50 caesarean section, 50 vaginal delivery) in government hospitals in Pali, Rajasthan, India
finding: Postnatal mothers who underwent caesarean section had poorer self-care practices initially compared to those who had vaginal delivery, but self-care practices improved daily due to education provided by healthcare personnel.
mod_finding: Mothers who underwent caesarean section had firmer and more retracted uteri on the first postnatal day compared to those with vaginal delivery; they also began self-care later.
